limits: These are repository-local benchmark and demo metrics, not independent third-party benchmarks.
Token estimates use a conservative character-to-token approximation of ceil(characters / 4).
Actual OpenAI token accounting depends on the provider tokenizer, model, request metadata, and generated output length.
The zero-token claim applies to existing-test review through the VS Code extension, CLI analyze, and CLI ci workflows.
The optional generate-and-check workflow still uses an LLM by design because it generates tests before checking them.

cases.description: A simple test imports and asserts behavior that exists in the source file.
cases.name: grounded_add

cases.description: A test imports a module that is not present in the source context.
cases.name: missing_import

cases.description: A test asserts a real failure path with pytest.raises and a built-in exception class.
cases.name: grounded_exception_path

cases.description: A repository test imports an existing private helper; this should be flagged as real evidence, not a missing symbol.
cases.name: private_helper_import

cases.description: A test constructs a real class and calls a real method on the instance.
cases.name: class_method_flow

cases.description: A test uses local variable names around a real source function; local names must not be treated as missing APIs.
cases.name: local_variables_not_missing_symbols

cases.description: A product-level test invents orchestration that low-level source helpers do not implement.
cases.name: invented_workflow

existing_test_review.token_cost_summary: The core review path uses local AST parsing, source-symbol checks, TF-IDF similarity, and optional pytest execution. It does not call OpenAI or any other LLM.
existing_test_review.workflow: VS Code extension, CLI analyze, and CLI ci for existing Python tests

optional_generation_token_estimate.why_this_matters: The optional generation workflow estimates file influence by re-running the model against different coalitions of uploaded files. Exact full enumeration is useful for tiny contexts, but it grows as 2^n. Counterfactual attribution keeps the request count roughly linear by comparing the full context to leave-one-file-out contexts plus the empty baseline.

product.name: Ghost Test Catcher
product.one_sentence_pitch: Ghost Test Catcher reviews Python tests against real source files so developers can spot grounded tests, salvageable tests, and ghost-risk tests before they merge AI-generated code.
primary_workflows: VS Code extension commands and Testing panel integration

safe_claims: Existing-test review in the VS Code extension, CLI analyze command, and CI gate uses 0 LLM calls and 0 estimated LLM tokens.
The built-in calibration suite matched expected verdicts on 7/7 scenarios in 2.401 seconds.
The demo project analysis reviewed 7 Python tests across 2 test files and 2 source files in 0.307 seconds with verdict 'reliable'.
For the optional 4-file generate-and-check sample, the attribution policy reduces estimated LLM calls from 16 to 6 (62.5% fewer calls).
For that same optional generation sample, estimated input tokens drop from 17881 to 8198 (54.2% fewer estimated input tokens).
